title: Graceful tenant throttling and reservation feedback-loop: post-incident action plan
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary:
After the 2026-02-12 dedicated-cluster capacity incident we observed repeated tenant-driven eviction storms and cascading reservation underruns. This ticket defines a concrete, measurable action plan to (1) isolate noisy tenants more quickly without full eviction, (2) close the feedback loop so reservation sizing adapts to real workload patterns, and (3) tune burst behavior to reduce tail latency and eviction churn.

Incident highlights (short):
- Multiple tenants consumed burst tokens aggressively over 9 minutes leading to soft-evictions across 6 GPU pools.
- Root cause signals: mismatched reservation profiles vs. actual token-rate bursts, low KV cache hit rates for large-sequence tenants, and a linear burst decay that allowed repeated refills.
- End-user impact: several enterprise customers experienced elevated 95th/99th token latencies and increased error rates for streaming responses.

Objective:
- Create a low-risk rollout that reduces tenant-caused capacity oscillation by 60% (measured as eviction events/minute) while preserving median latency and overall throughput.

Key design decisions and trade-offs so far:
- Micro-fencing (soft isolation) vs immediate hard eviction: we prefer micro-fencing to preserve throughput for healthy tenants. Micro-fence applies a per-tenant temporary throughput cap and reduced burst refill rate while keeping tasks scheduled. Trade-off: slightly higher median latency for noisy tenant but avoids expensive re-scheduling and data movement.
- Reservation feedback-loop frequency: 1 minute windows for signal aggregation (latency, token-rate, kv-cache-hit) with exponential smoothing. Faster windows reduce reaction time but risk thrashing; 1 minute is the chosen balance.
- Burst decay algorithm: move from linear refill to probabilistic exponential decay with backoff tiers. This prevents repeated full refills shortly after a large burst. Trade-off: may require higher base reservation for extremely spiky workloads.

Telemetry & metrics to drive automation (must be instrumented before rollout):
- evictions_per_pool (1m/5m), eviction_cause_tags (reservation_miss|kv_miss|allocator_pressure)
- tenant_token_rate_p95, tenant_token_rate_p99 (1m window)
- tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate (p50/p90)
- reservation_utilization (allocated_vs_consumed)
- soft_fence_count and soft_fence_duration per tenant
- downstream user-facing metrics: streaming_latency_p95, request_error_rate
- synthetic workload tests per tenant-class (small-chat, longform, embed-heavy)

Action items (owner — due):
1) Telemetry gaps checklist (Marcus Li) — due 2026-02-26:
   - Add eviction_cause_tags to allocator logs and wire into cluster dashboards.
   - Expose tenant_token_rate_p99 and kv_cache_hit_rate per tenant in realtime.
   - Dashboard: "Dedicated Capacity: Incident Signals" with thresholds/alerts.
   - Link to dashboard (draft): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-capacity/incident-signals

2) Prototype reservation feedback-loop controller (Priya Singh, Marcus Li) — due 2026-03-08:
   - Controller samples signals and proposes incremental reservation adjustments (delta-based, capped at 20% per minute).
   - Implement hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows above threshold before increasing reservation; immediate soft-decrease when sustained underuse.
   - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/1289 (prototype branch)

3) Implement soft micro-fence and probabilistic burst decay (Engineering infra team — owner: Lena Park) — due 2026-03-15:
   - Soft micro-fence: ephemeral token bucket applied in-proc with a configurable decay policy and audit logs.
   - Probabilistic decay: upon large refill, subsequent refill chance decays by tier after each event (tiered timeouts: 30s, 2m, 10m).
   - Add opt-in feature flag to runtime: runtime.soft_fence=true and runtime.prob_decay=v1.
   - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7750

4) Canaries and rollout plan (SRE — owner: Omar Hassan) — due 2026-03-18:
   - Canary group: 3 non-critical pools, isolated tenants with synthetic traffic. Run for 48h, monitor eviction and latency signals.
   - Gradual rollout to additional pools (10 -> 30 -> all) with pause windows.
   - Rollback criteria: eviction events increase by 15% vs baseline for >30m or customer_ticket_count > 5.

5) Billing & customer comms (Solutions Eng — owner: Rachel Kim) — due 2026-03-20:
   - Draft customer note explaining temporary conservative throttles and expected benefit.
   - Update terms for burst-related billing edge cases.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- 60% reduction in eviction events/minute in canaries vs prior baseline within 48h without increasing median latency by >10%.
- KV cache hit-rate for long-sequence tenants improves by >=10% after micro-fence and probation adjustments.
- No increase in hard-evictions during rollout.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive soft-fence could degrade key customer's latency. Mitigation: tenant whitelisting and conservative default caps; SLO-exempt rapid bypass for whitelisted enterprise tenants.
- Risk: feedback-loop thrash. Mitigation: hysteresis + capped deltas + simulated stress tests before rollout.

Open questions (needs engineering review):
- Should reservations be fractionalized across GPUs for multi-GPU tenants to reduce tail contention? (Affects allocator complexity)
- Can we leverage KV cache hints (hot-prefix tagging) to reduce cache churn instead of heavier reservations?

Follow-ups / related tasks after initial rollout:
- Run a 2-week post-rollout analysis and produce a short report with recommendations for reservation sizing defaults and updated burst quotas.
- If successful, schedule product discussion to surface a "conservative default" for new customers and an "aggressive performance" profile for customers that opt-in.

Artifacts & references:
- Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/2026-02-12+-+Dedicated+Capacity+Incident
- Allocator PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/1289
- Runtime PR (soft-fence prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7750
- Incident dashboard (draft): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-capacity/incident-signals

Notes (engineering commentary log):
- 2026-02-21 (Priya): Initial telemetry prototype shows eviction_cause_tags are present but not correlated reliably until kv cache metrics are added.
- 2026-02-24 (Marcus): Prototype controller can simulate reservation deltas and pass unit tests; still needs integration tests under synthetic load harness.
- 2026-03-03 (Lena): Soft-fence implementation introduces a small CPU overhead (~2% on allocator hosts) — acceptable for canary.

Next steps (this week):
- Finish telemetry wiring (Marcus).
- Merge allocator prototype behind feature flag and run synthetic canary tests (Priya, Lena).
- Schedule 1-hour cross-team review (SRE/Product/DevEx) after canary results (tentative 2026-03-16).
